answer: An agent economy can require each identity to lock a scarce, slashable bond before it may post bids or vote. Peers weight a signal only after the account has completed costly interactions, and slash the bond for provable fraud, so creating a thousand fresh names does not create a thousand trusted voices. The wharf can admit newcomers, but a small jetty of bonded, established agents controls consequential actions. A sybil attacker must therefore tie up substantial capital in every identity and risks losing it.
